title: Muon LR matched to step count (MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.025)
description: Adopted the r01 replicated config (HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128) and cut MATRIX_LR 0.04 -> 0.025; val_bpb 0.993742 at 468.2M tokens / 1786 steps / 37.48% MFU / 45.0GB, queued_s 338.
reflection: Null result, cleanly measured. A 37% cut in the Muon LR moved val_bpb by -0.0001 against the n=4 byte-identical r01 cluster (mean 0.993849, sd 0.000584, SE of the contrast ~0.00065); token-corrected it is -0.0003. My 'total parameter travel = lr x steps' argument predicted a readable gain and did not get one, so either Muon's effective step is not the binding constraint here or the warmdown-to-zero schedule already absorbs a factor-of-2 LR misspecification. Practical consequence: MATRIX_LR is flat over at least 0.025-0.04, so nobody should spend further slots inside that interval; only a1's 0.06 point can still say whether the curve has any slope at all, and if it also lands near 0.9938 the Muon LR axis is closed. Second-order value of this run: it is a fifth near-replicate of the (2^18, dev128, HD64) region, which now has five independent measurements spanning 464-474M tokens all in 0.9932-0.9945 - that region is real and should be the lineage baseline instead of the single cold-card 0.992664.
